summary: ```markdown # CLO2024.2 - GPU Simulation ## Overview of Improvements In the 2022.4.2 version, we improved the conflict processing function of GPU simulation. This enhancement allows for stable simulation when simulating the clothing of multi-layered plates. Additionally, the conflict processing between the plate and the virtual model can be run smoothly, increasing the efficiency of the work. ## UI Changes Let's take a closer look at the improvements through the example. We have improved the menu of simulation functions since GPU simulation has been enhanced and the scope of use expanded. ### New Features in the Menu - **Animation Recording**: Added animation used when recording animation, complete with image. - **CPU and GPU Options**: A menu for setting CPU and GPU options has been added at the bottom of the simulation type. It allows for setting CPU and GPU options for ordinary, test, and animation simulation, respectively. When the GPU option is set, the simulation icons are displayed as empty keys. ## Performance Comparison Next, let's compare the use of GPU and CPU. To make a clear comparison, you can click on the main menu to set the display environment to "display real speed," which shows the information and FPS speed of the used version at the bottom left of the 3D window. ### Simulation Speed First, we will compare the simulation speed of normal speed and default. On the left is GPU, and on the right is CPU. You can see that in terms of speed, the GPU simulation is much faster. Next, we will use the test穿 to simulate. Similarly, we can see that GPU simulation is much faster than CPU simulation. Please note that GPU simulation speed may depend on the performance of the graphics card. ## Stability of Simulation After choosing GPU simulation, we can pull the board in the 3D window to observe the stability of the simulation. Even with a multi-layer board, it can be simulated in a stable manner. ### Animation Mode Demonstration Next, we will demonstrate the process of using GPU simulation in animation mode to record the process of having multi-layer board clothing. Once again, after selecting GPU simulation, we can pull the board in the 3D window to observe the stability of the simulation. When the strength of the Agreed loss of factor is relatively small and the number of boards and layers is increased, it is much faster and more stable to use GPU simulation than before. However, this may also be attributed to the performance of the graphics card. ## Limitations of GPU Simulation It should be noted that GPU simulation is currently only applicable to ordinary clothing simulation and does not include wool products. Additionally, it is not currently applicable to secondary simulation and software model simulation. ## Accuracy Improvements In addition to improving the speed of simulation, the enhancement of conflict processing has also improved the accuracy of GPU simulation. When using GPU simulation, it can yield results comparable to those of CPU simulation. ### Project File Saving Please note that when saving project files, the option of not saving the processor should not be selected. For example, when saving this file, if the CPU is selected, the GPU simulation mode changes to the GPU normal mode in the software. When the file is opened again, it will revert to the processor option selected at that time. However, the normal test mode and animation simulation options are saved in the file mode and become the test mode. ## Conclusion After these improvements, the GPU simulation can now be stabilized and simulated quickly. We welcome you to experience GPU simulation. Thank you for your attention. Please write your feelings and suggestions in the message area. ```
